# Test that calling t.Fatal in a benchmark causes a non-zero exit status.

! go test -run '^$' -bench '^BenchmarkThatCallsFatal$' benchfatal
! stdout ^ok
! stderr ^ok
stdout FAIL.*benchfatal

# A failure after the first run must reach both B.Run and the process exit status.
go test -c -o benchfatal.test$GOEXE benchfatal
! exec ./benchfatal.test$GOEXE -test.bench=BenchmarkFatalOnRepeat -test.benchtime=1x -test.count=2
stdout '^B.Run returned false$'
! exec ./benchfatal.test$GOEXE -test.bench=BenchmarkFatalOnRepeat -test.benchtime=1x -test.cpu=1,2
stdout '^B.Run returned false$'

-- go.mod --
module benchfatal

go 1.16
-- x_test.go --
package benchfatal

import (
	"fmt"
	"testing"
)

func BenchmarkThatCallsFatal(b *testing.B) {
	b.Fatal("called by benchmark")
}

func BenchmarkFatalOnRepeat(b *testing.B) {
	var calls int
	ok := b.Run("sub", func(b *testing.B) {
		calls++
		if calls == 2 {
			b.Fatal("second run")
		}
	})
	fmt.Println("B.Run returned", ok)
}
